transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Hello, Dr. Smith. Any time I have to get blood drawn, I go to great lengths to avoid it or sit there in sheer terror the whole time. It has just become too much for me to handle on my own.
When you are in those situations, do you ever experience a drop in blood pressure that causes you to feel faint or actually lose consciousness?

Yes, I absolutely do. About a year ago, I actually fainted and fell during a routine blood test, which ended up breaking my wrist. Now, even just seeing a picture of a blood draw makes me feel that same swooping light-headedness, as if I might pass out all over again.
Besides the fear of the blood draw itself, are there any other specific situations, such as receiving an injection or seeing an injury, that trigger this same fainting response?

I'm not really sure about those other things, to be honest. My fear and that awful light-headed feeling are really focused specifically on blood draws, where they put a needle into my vein to take blood. I haven't really noticed having that same reaction to regular injections or seeing injuries.
